title: Admit a locale before loading a server dictionary
businessContext: Review a focused Next.js application change before it reaches production. The proposed file below contains the defect or unsupported assumption; external application services, where imported, are integration boundaries.
problemStatement: Review the proposed app/[lang]/page.tsx change. Identify the incorrect framework assumption, propose a minimal corrected implementation, and provide evidence for the selected version scope and its 15/16 differences. Explain the interview variation after solving the base task. This is a framework code review: actual rendering, routing and cache behavior must be checked in a real Next.js build, not a browser function sandbox.
starterCode:
export default async function Page({params}:any){const dictionary=await import('../../dictionaries/'+params.lang+'.json');return

{dictionary.title}

;}

constraints: Preserve the stated user behavior and keep trust boundaries explicit.
Use the selected version’s documented API; do not suppress build/type failures to hide the defect.
Request en, hi and an unsupported locale.
Verify the browser does not download every complete dictionary unnecessarily.
Test canonical/hreflang metadata and any locale redirect loop policy in a real deployment.
candidateTasks: Add actionable line-level review comments explaining impact and correction.
Write the corrected file in the local IDE copy; split annotated companion files where instructed.
Record actual build/request/navigation evidence against the acceptance checks and compare version notes.
hints: An admitted locale selects a known loader instead of constructing an arbitrary module path from a route parameter.

alternativeApproaches: No. Language negotiation is a representation preference, not identity or domain ownership. Keep trusted tenant/domain resolution separate and include admitted locale in any shared representation key.
commonMistakes: Verifying only next dev when the behavior depends on production rendering or bundling.
Treating a visible UI state, matcher or TypeScript type as a substitute for server-side validation and authorization.
